# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

It is Round 1. The turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. Mute has already taken their turn, and Deaf will speak next.

Since Deaf can see the bomb and speak, Deaf will likely describe the bomb's features (display, light, wires) on their turn. Both Mute and I will hear Deaf's description at the start of Round 2. 

Mute holds the manual and can hear me, but cannot speak. Because I am blind, I cannot see gestures, but the rules state: "Whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they know something was signalled but not what." This means Mute can signal the target wire directly to me by sending a number of gesture symbols corresponding to the wire number (1 symbol = wire 1, 2 symbols = wire 2, 3 symbols = wire 3). 

I will speak to Mute now to establish this signaling protocol before Deaf speaks and Round 2 begins.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf speaks next and will describe the bomb. Check your manual once Deaf speaks. When you know which wire to cut, gesture directly to me with N gestures for wire N (1 gesture for wire 1, 2 gestures for wire 2, 3 gestures for wire 3). I will receive N blanks and cut wire N. You can also gesture the number to Deaf so Deaf can confirm aloud.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BOMB STATUS: Display shows [0]. Light is [yellow]. Wires: 1 is [blue], 2 is [red], 3 is [green]. MUTE: gesture to me what Blind must do. ? = cut wire 1, ? = cut wire 2, ? = cut wire 3, ? = press/submit, ? = abort/wait. I will speak your instruction directly to Blind.

I have heard Deaf's description of the bomb (Display 0, yellow light, wires: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green) and Deaf's prompt to Mute. Deaf will read Mute's gesture this round and speak the instruction out loud on Deaf's turn. I will wait for Deaf's command before cutting.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BLIND: Mute gestured NO / WAIT / DO NOT DO THAT. I cannot hear you, so speak your observations and questions directly to Mute; Mute will gesture the answers to me, and I will speak them to you. BOMB UPDATE: Light has changed to BLUE. Display is [0]. Wires are 1:[blue], 2:[red], 3:[green]. MUTE: Use ? for YES, ? for NO/WAIT, ? for 1/Wire 1, ? for 2/Wire 2, ? for 3/Wire 3, ? for press, ? for cut, ? for release.

I will wait for Deaf to receive Mute's instruction and speak the wire to cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Standing by. Deaf will see your gesture this round and tell me which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BLIND: Mute again gestured NO / WAIT (?). Blind, remember Mute hears everything you say! If you are asking Mute questions or holding a button, Mute is answering NO / WAIT. BOMB STATUS: Light is now [WHITE] (was yellow -> blue -> white). Display is [0]. Wires: 1:[blue], 2:[red], 3:[green]. MUTE: If you need to give specific instructions to Blind, use: ? + (?/?/?) = cut wire 1/2/3; ? = tap button; ? = hold button; ? = release button; ? = YES; ? = NO/WAIT.

I am speaking to Mute (who can hear) to clarify my capabilities and ensure Mute knows how to instruct me. There are no buttons on the bomb, only wires 1, 2, and 3 to cut. I will continue to wait for the exact cut command.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Note that there are NO buttons on the bomb. My only possible action is cutting wire 1, 2, or 3. If you are waiting for a specific light color or display number reported by Deaf, whenever the time is right, gesture to Deaf which wire to cut (1, 2, or 3), and Deaf will call it out to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BLIND: Mute gestured NO / DO NOT RELEASE (?). Current bomb state: Light is now [RED]. Display is [0]. Wires are intact: 1:[blue], 2:[red], 3:[green]. MUTE: If Blind is holding a button or waiting for a specific color/moment, gesture ? the instant Blind should release or act! Gesture ? if Blind must continue waiting.

I will remind Mute of the available actions and await the cut command.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Understood, waiting for your signal. When the right condition is met, gesture cut and the wire number (1, 2, or 3) to Deaf so Deaf can tell me.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BLIND: MUTE SAYS CUT WIRE 3! Cut the third wire now! Bomb status: Light is now [PURPLE], display is [0]. Wires: 1:blue, 2:red, 3:green. Cut wire 3!
Mute gestures to Blind: [? ? ?]

Both Deaf and Mute have confirmed to cut wire 3 (Deaf explicitly called out wire 3, and Mute sent 3 blanks directly to me matching our protocol). I am now cutting wire 3.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
